2014_spells.etherealness.description:
As an action, you step into the border regions of the Ethereal Plane in the area where it overlaps with your current plane. You remain in the Border Ethereal for the duration of 8 hours or until you use your action to dismiss the spell. During this time, you can move in any direction; however, moving up or down costs an extra foot of movement for every foot traveled. You can see and hear the plane you originated from, though everything appears gray and visibility is limited to 60 feet.

While on the Ethereal Plane, you can only affect and be affected by other creatures on that plane. Creatures not on the Ethereal Plane cannot perceive or interact with you unless they have a special ability or magic to do so. You ignore all objects and effects not on the Ethereal Plane, allowing you to move through objects you perceive on your plane of origin.

When the spell ends, you immediately return to the plane you originated from in your current spot. If you occupy the same spot as a solid object or creature, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take force damage equal to twice the number of feet you are moved.

This spell has no effect if cast while you are already on the Ethereal Plane or a plane that does not border it, such as one of the Outer Planes.

2014_spells.finger-of-death.description:
Using 1 action, you send negative energy coursing through a creature you can see within 60 feet, causing it searing pain. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. It takes **7d8 + 30** necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

A humanoid killed by this spell rises at the start of your next turn as a zombie that is permanently under your command, following your verbal orders to the best of its ability.
2014_spells.finger-of-death.effectSummar: Blast a target with negative energy to deal massive necrotic damage, with the added effect of raising any killed humanoid as a loyal zombie.

2014_spells.fire-storm.description:
As an action, a storm made up of sheets of roaring flame appears in a location you choose within 150 feet. The area of the storm consists of up to ten 10-foot cubes, which you can arrange as you wish, provided each cube has at least one face adjacent to the face of another cube. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. It takes **7d10** fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

The fire damages objects in the area and ignites flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried. If you choose, plant life in the area is unaffected by this spell.
2014_spells.fire-storm.effectSummary: Create a massive storm of roaring flames in a customizable area to incinerate enemies and ignite flammable objects within a wide range.

2014_spells.forcecage.description:
As an action, you create an immobile, invisible, cube-shaped prison composed of magical force within 100 feet. The prison lasts for 1 hour and can be created in one of two forms:

- A cage: Up to 20 feet on a side, consisting of 1/2-inch diameter bars spaced 1/2 inch apart.
- A solid box: Up to 10 feet on a side, creating a solid barrier that prevents any matter from passing through and blocks any spells cast into or out of the area.

When you cast the spell, any creature completely inside the area is trapped. Creatures only partially within the area, or those too large to fit, are pushed away from the center until they are completely outside. 

A creature inside the cage cannot leave by nonmagical means. If a creature attempts to use teleportation or interplanar travel to exit, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a success, the creature exits the cage; on a failure, the creature remains trapped and wastes the use of the spell or effect. The cage also extends into the Ethereal Plane, blocking ethereal travel. This spell cannot be dispelled by dispel magic.
2014_spells.forcecage.effectSummary: Create an immobile, invisible prison of magical force to trap creatures within a designated area, preventing nonmagical escape and blocking certain teleportation.

2014_spells.magnificent-mansion.descript:
Using a casting time of 1 minute, you conjure an extradimensional dwelling within 300 feet that lasts for 24 hours. You choose the location of its single entrance, which is 5 feet wide and 10 feet tall. You and any creatures you designate upon casting can enter the dwelling while the portal is open. You can open or close the portal if you are within 30 feet of it; while closed, the portal is invisible.

Beyond the portal is a magnificent foyer with numerous chambers. You can create any floor plan you like, provided the space does not exceed 50 cubes (each 10 feet on each side). The mansion is furnished and decorated as you choose and contains enough food to serve a nine-course banquet for up to 100 people.

A staff of 100 near-transparent servants, whose appearance and attire you decide, attend to all who enter. These servants are completely obedient and can perform any task a normal human servant could, such as fetching items, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, and pouring wine. However, they cannot attack or take any action that would directly harm another creature. Servants can go anywhere in the mansion but cannot leave it. 

Furnishings and other objects created by this spell dissipate into smoke if removed from the mansion. When the spell ends, any creatures inside the extradimensional space are expelled into the open spaces nearest to the entrance.

2014_spells.mirage-arcane.description:
Over the course of 10 minutes, you make terrain in an area up to 1 mile square within sight look, sound, smell, and even feel like some other sort of terrain for a duration of 10 days. While the general shape of the terrain remains the same, you can make open fields or roads resemble swamps, hills, crevasses, or other difficult or impassable terrain. Similarly, a pond can seem like a grassy meadow, a precipice like a gentle slope, or a rock-strewn gully like a wide, smooth road.

You can also alter the appearance of structures or add them where none exist, though the spell does not disguise, conceal, or add creatures.

The illusion includes audible, visual, tactile, and olfactory elements, allowing it to turn clear ground into difficult terrain (or vice versa) or otherwise impede movement. Any piece of illusory terrain, such as a rock or stick, disappears immediately if removed from the spell's area.

Creatures with truesight can see through the illusion to the terrain's true form; however, all other elements of the illusion remain, meaning the creature is aware of the illusion but can still physically interact with it.

2014_spells.plane-shift.description:
As an action, you and up to eight willing creatures who link hands in a circle are transported to a different plane of existence. You can specify a target destination in general terms, and you appear in or near that destination at the GM's discretion. Alternatively, if you know the sigil sequence of a teleportation circle on another plane of existence, this spell can take you to that circle; if the circle is too small, creatures appear in the closest unoccupied spaces next to it.

You can also use this spell to banish an unwilling creature to another plane. Choose a creature within your touch range and make a melee spell attack against it. On a hit, the creature must make a Charisma saving throw. If the creature fails this save, it is transported to a random location on the plane of existence you specify and must find its own way back to your current plane.

2014_spells.power-word-pain-2.descriptio: You speak a word of power that causes waves of intense pain to assail one creature you can see within range. If the target has 100 hit points or fewer, it is subject to crippling pain. Otherwise, the spell has no effect on it.

2014_spells.prismatic-spray.description:

- Red: The target takes **10d6** fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
- Orange: The target takes **10d6** acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
- Yellow: The target takes **10d6** lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
- Green: The target takes **10d6** poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
- Blue: The target takes **10d6** cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
- Indigo: On a failed save, the target is restrained. It must then make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. If it successfully saves three times, the spell ends. If it fails its save three times, it permanently turns to stone and is subjected to the petrified condition.
- Violet: On a failed save, the target is blinded. It must then make a Wisdom saving throw at the start of your next turn. A successful save ends the blindness. If it fails that save, the creature is transported to another plane of existence of the GM's choosing and is no longer blinded.
- Special: The target is struck by two rays. Roll twice more, rerolling any 8.

2014_spells.project-image.description:
As an action, you create an illusory copy of yourself that lasts for a duration of up to 24 hours. The copy can appear at any location within 500 miles that you have seen before, regardless of intervening obstacles. The illusion looks and sounds like you but is intangible; if the illusion takes any damage, it disappears and the spell ends.

- You can use your action to move this illusion up to twice your speed and make it gesture, speak, and behave in whatever way you choose.
- You can see through its eyes and hear through its ears as if you were in its space. As a bonus action on your turn, you can switch between using its senses and your own. While using its senses, you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings.
- Physical interaction reveals the image to be an illusion. A creature using its action to examine the image can determine it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC. Once discerned, the creature can see through the image and any noise it makes sounds hollow.
2014_spells.project-image.effectSummary: Create an intangible illusory duplicate of yourself at a distant location to scout and communicate while observing through its senses.

2014_spells.regenerate.description:
With a casting time of 1 minute, you touch a creature to stimulate its natural healing ability. The target immediately regains **4d8 + 15** hit points. For the duration of 1 hour, the target regains 1 hit point at the start of each of its turns (10 hit points each minute).

- Severed body members (such as fingers, legs, or tails) are restored after 2 minutes.
- If you hold the severed part to the stump, the spell instantaneously causes the limb to knit to the stump.
2014_spells.regenerate.effectSummary: Touch a creature to provide immediate healing and a sustained recovery effect that can restore severed limbs over time.

2014_spells.resurrection.description:
Using a casting time of 1 hour, you touch a dead creature that has been dead for no more than a century, did not die of old age, and is not undead. If its soul is free and willing, the target returns to life with all its hit points. This effect is instantaneous.

- The spell neutralizes any poisons and cures normal diseases present at the time of death, though magical diseases and curses remain.
- All mortal wounds are closed and missing body parts are restored.
- The target suffers a -4 penalty to all attack rolls, saving throws, and ability checks. This penalty is reduced by 1 every time the target finishes a long rest until it disappears.
- If the creature has been dead for one year or longer, you are greatly taxed until you finish a long rest: you cannot cast spells and have disadvantage on all attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
2014_spells.resurrection.effectSummary: Bring a dead creature back to life with full hit points, provided they have been dead for no more than a century and their soul is willing.
2014_spells.resurrection.fullDescription:

2014_spells.reverse-gravity.description:
As an action, you reverse gravity in a 50-foot-radius, 100-foot high cylinder centered on a point within 100 feet. All creatures and objects that aren't somehow anchored to the ground in the area fall upward and reach the top of the area when you cast this spell. A creature can make a Dexterity saving throw to grab onto a fixed object it can reach, thus avoiding the fall.

- If some solid object (such as a ceiling) is encountered in this fall, falling objects and creatures strike it just as they would during a normal downward fall.
- If an object or creature reaches the top of the area without striking anything, it remains there, oscillating slightly, for the duration.

At the end of the duration, affected objects and creatures fall back down.
2014_spells.reverse-gravity.effectSummar: Reverses gravity within a massive cylindrical area, causing unanchored creatures and objects to fall upward and remain suspended until the spell ends.
2014_spells.reverse-gravity.fullDescript:
As an action, you reverse gravity in a 50-foot-radius, 100-foot high cylinder centered on a point within 100 feet. All creatures and objects that aren't somehow anchored to the ground in the area fall upward and reach the top of the area when you cast this spell. A creature can make a Dexterity saving throw to grab onto a fixed object it can reach, thus avoiding the fall.

- If some solid object (such as a ceiling) is encountered in this fall, falling objects and creatures strike it just as they would during a normal downward fall.
- If an object or creature reaches the top of the area without striking anything, it remains there, oscillating slightly, for the duration.

At the end of the duration, affected objects and creatures fall back down.
2014_spells.sequester.description:
As an action, you touch a willing creature or an object to hide it away, safe from detection for the duration. The target becomes invisible and cannot be targeted by divination spells or perceived through scrying sensors created by divination spells.

- If the target is a creature, it falls into a state of suspended animation. Time ceases to flow for it, and it doesn't grow older.

You can set a condition for the spell to end early. The condition can be anything you choose, but it must occur or be visible within 1 mile of the target. Examples include "after 1,000 years" or "when the tarrasque awakens." This spell also ends if the target takes any damage.

2014_spells.simulacrum.description:
Over a casting time of 12 hours, you shape an illusory duplicate of one beast or humanoid that is within touch range for the entire duration of the casting. The duplicate is a creature, partially real and formed from ice or snow, and it can take actions and otherwise be affected as a normal creature. It appears to be the same as the original, but it has half the creature's hit point maximum and is formed without any equipment. Otherwise, the illusion uses all the statistics of the creature it duplicates.

- The simulacrum is friendly to you and creatures you designate. It obeys your spoken commands, moving and acting in accordance with your wishes and acting on your turn in combat.
- The simulacrum lacks the ability to learn or become more powerful, so it never increases its level or other abilities, nor can it regain expended spell slots.
- If the simulacrum is damaged, you can repair it in an alchemical laboratory, using rare herbs and minerals worth 100 gp per hit point it regains.
- The simulacrum lasts until it drops to 0 hit points, at which point it reverts to snow and melts instantly.

If you cast this spell again, any currently active duplicates you created with this spell are instantly destroyed.

2014_spells.symbol.description:
Using a casting time of 1 minute, you inscribe a harmful glyph at a range of touch, either on a surface (up to 10 feet in diameter) or within a closable object. If an object is moved more than 10 feet from where the spell was cast, the glyph is broken and the spell ends.

The glyph is nearly invisible and requires an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to find. You define the trigger upon casting, such as touching the glyph, opening the object, or specific creature characteristics. 

Once triggered, the glyph glows, filling a 60-foot-radius sphere with dim light for 10 minutes. Each creature in the sphere when it activates, or any creature that enters or ends its turn there, is targeted by one of the following effects:

- Death: The target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking **10d10** necrotic damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
- Discord: The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it bickers for 1 minute, losing the ability to communicate meaningfully and gaining disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
- Fear: The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is frightened for 1 minute, drops its held items, and must move at least 30 feet away from the glyph on each turn.
- Hopelessness: The target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is overwhelmed with despair for 1 minute and cannot attack or target others with harmful abilities, spells, or magical effects.
- Insanity: The target must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, it is insane for 1 minute, cannot take actions, cannot read or understand others, and speaks only in gibberish while the GM controls its erratic movement.
- Pain: The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it is incapacitated by excruciating pain for 1 minute.
- Sleep: The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it falls unconscious for 10 minutes, awakening if it takes damage or is shaken awake.
- Stunning: The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is stunned for 1 minute.

2014_spells.teleport.description:
With a casting time of 1 action, you can instantly transport yourself and up to eight willing creatures you can see within a range of 10 feet, or a single object you can see within that range, to a destination on the same plane. Objects must fit in a 10-foot cube and cannot be held by an unwilling creature.

Success depends on your familiarity with the destination, determined by a d100 roll:

- Permanent circle or Associated object: Always on target.
- Very familiar: 25% on target, 21% off target, 8% similar area, 5% mishap.
- Seen casually: 46% on target, 10% off target, 10% similar area, 33% mishap.
- Viewed once or Description: 26% on target, 20% off target, 10% similar area, 43% mishap.
- False destination: 50% similar area, 50% mishap.

Outcomes include:

- On Target: You arrive exactly where intended.
- Off Target: You appear a random distance away. This distance is **1d10** x **1d10** percent of the total travel distance, with the direction determined by a d8 roll.
- Similar Area: You appear in the closest visually or thematically similar location on the plane.
- Mishap: Each teleporting creature or object takes **3d10** force damage, and the GM rerolls on the table to determine the final destination; multiple mishaps can occur.

2014_spells.whirlwind.fullDescription: Using 1 action, a whirlwind howls down to a point on the ground you can see within range. Until the spell ends, you can use your action to move the whirlwind up to 30 feet in any direction along the ground; you must concentrate, and the effect ends if your concentration ends.
Deal 12d8 necrotic damage to a target within 150 ft

Using 1 action, you draw the moisture from every creature in a 30-foot cube centered on a point you choose within range. A creature takes 12d8 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one; Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw; roll a d20, add the CON modifier, and compare it with your spell save spell save DC. Nonmagical plants in the area that aren't creatures, such as trees and crops, are instantly withered and destroyed.
2014_spells.animal-shapes.description:
Using 1 action, you can use your magic to turn any number of willing creatures you can see within 30 feet into beasts. Each target is transformed into the form of a Large or smaller beast with a challenge rating of 4 or lower. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to transform affected creatures into new forms.

The transformation lasts for the duration of up to 24 hours, or until the target drops to 0 hit points or dies. You can choose a different form for each target. A target's game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the chosen beast, though the target retains its alignment and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.

- The target assumes the hit points of its new form. When it reverts to its normal form, it returns to the number of hit points it had before it transformed.
- If it reverts as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce the creature's normal form to 0 hit points, it isn't knocked unconscious.
- The creature is limited in the actions it can perform by the nature of its new form, and it can't speak or cast spells.
- The target's gear melds into the new form, and the target cannot activate, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its equipment.

2014_spells.antimagic-field.description:
As 1 action, you create a 10-foot-radius invisible sphere of antimagic centered on yourself that moves with you for a duration of up to 1 hour. Within this sphere, spells cannot be cast, summoned creatures disappear, and magic items become mundane. Spells and other magical effects, except those created by an artifact or a deity, are suppressed in the sphere and cannot protrude into it. A slot expended to cast a suppressed spell is consumed; while suppressed, the effect does not function, but the time spent suppressed counts against its duration.

- Targeted Effects: Spells and other magical effects, such as magic missile and charm person, that target a creature or an object in the sphere have no effect on that target.
- Areas of Magic: The area of another spell or magical effect, such as fireball, cannot extend into the sphere. If the sphere overlaps an area of magic, the covered part is suppressed (e.g., creating a gap in a wall of fire).
- Spells: Any active spell or other magical effect on a creature or an object in the sphere is suppressed while the creature or object is in it.
- Magic Items: The properties and powers of magic items are suppressed. A +1 longsword functions as a nonmagical longsword. A magic weapon's powers are suppressed if used against a target in the sphere or wielded by an attacker in the sphere. If a magic weapon or piece of magic ammunition fully leaves the sphere, its magic ceases to be suppressed.
- Magical Travel: Teleportation and planar travel fail to work in the sphere, whether as the destination or departure point. Portals to other locations, worlds, or planes, and openings to extradimensional spaces (such as those created by the rope trick spell), temporarily close.
- Creatures and Objects: A creature or object summoned or created by magic temporarily winks out of existence in the sphere and reappears once the space it occupied is no longer within the sphere.
- Dispel Magic: Spells and magical effects such as dispel magic have no effect on the sphere, and spheres created by different antimagic field spells do not nullify each other.

2014_spells.antipathy-sympathy.descripti:
Over the course of a 1 hour casting time, you target something within 60 feet—either a Huge or smaller object or creature, or an area no larger than a 200-foot cube—and specify a kind of intelligent creature. You invest the target with an aura that lasts for 10 days, choosing either antipathy or sympathy as the effect:

- Antipathy: Creatures of the designated kind that can see the target or come within 60 feet of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened. While frightened, the creature must use its movement to move to the nearest safe spot from which it cannot see the target. If the creature moves more than 60 feet away and cannot see the target, it is no longer frightened, though it becomes so again if it regains sight or moves within 60 feet.
- Sympathy: Creatures of the designated kind that can see the target or come within 60 feet of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or use its movement on each of its turns to enter the area or move within reach of the target. Once it has done so, it cannot willingly move away.

If the target harms an affected creature, that creature can make a Wisdom saving throw to end the effect. Additionally, if an affected creature ends its turn while not within 60 feet of the target or able to see it, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the creature is no longer affected and recognizes the magic. Affected creatures are allowed another Wisdom saving throw every 24 hours. A creature that successfully saves is immune for 1 minute.

2014_spells.clone.description:
Using a 1 hour casting time and a touch range, you grow an inert duplicate of a living creature inside a sealed vessel. The clone grows to full size and maturity after 120 days, though you may choose to have it be a younger version of the creature. The clone remains inert and endures indefinitely as long as the vessel is undisturbed.

At any time after the clone matures, if the original creature dies, its soul transfers to the clone, provided the soul is free and willing to return. The clone is physically identical to the original and possesses the same personality, memories, and abilities, but it does not have any of the original's equipment. The original creature's physical remains become inert and cannot be restored to life, as the soul now resides in the clone. The spell's duration is instantaneous.

2014_spells.control-weather.description:
With a casting time of 10 minutes, you take control of the weather within 5 miles of yourself for up to 8 hours. You must be outdoors to cast this spell, and moving to a place without a clear path to the sky ends the spell early.

You can change the current precipitation, temperature, and wind. It takes **1d4 x 10** minutes for new conditions to take effect, after which you can change them again. When the spell ends, the weather gradually returns to normal. You change conditions by shifting the current stage up or down by one on the following tables:

- Precipitation: 1. Clear, 2. Light clouds, 3. Overcast or ground fog, 4. Rain, hail, or snow, 5. Torrential rain, driving hail, or blizzard.
- Temperature: 1. Unbearable heat, 2. Hot, 3. Warm, 4. Cool, 5. Cold, 6. Arctic cold.
- Wind: 1. Calm, 2. Moderate wind, 3. Strong wind, 4. Gale, 5. Storm. (You may also change the wind direction).

2014_spells.demiplane.description:
As an action, you create a shadowy door on a flat solid surface that you can see within 60 feet. The door is large enough to allow Medium creatures to pass through unhindered. When opened, the door leads to a demiplane that appears to be an empty room 30 feet in each dimension, made of wood or stone.

When the spell ends after 1 hour, the door disappears, and any creatures or objects inside the demiplane remain trapped there, as the door also disappears from the other side.

Each time you cast this spell, you can:
- Create a new demiplane.
- Have the shadowy door connect to a demiplane you created with a previous casting of this spell.
- Connect to a demiplane created by another creature, provided you know the nature and contents of that demiplane.

2014_spells.dominate-monster.description:
As an action, you attempt to beguile a creature that you can see within 60 feet. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for a duration of up to 1 hour. If you or creatures that are friendly to you are fighting it, the target has advantage on the saving throw.

While the creature is charmed, you have a telepathic link with it as long as the two of you are on the same plane of existence. You can use this link to issue commands to the creature while you are conscious (no action required), which it does its best to obey. You can specify a simple and general course of action, such as "Attack that creature," "Run over there," or "Fetch that object." If the creature completes the order and doesn't receive further direction from you, it defends and preserves itself to the best of its ability.

You can use your action to take total and precise control of the target. Until the end of your next turn, the creature takes only the actions you choose and doesn't do anything that you don't allow it to do. During this time, you can also cause the creature to use a reaction, but this requires you to use your own reaction as well.

Each time the target takes damage, it makes a new Wisdom saving throw against the spell. If the saving throw succeeds, the spell ends.

2014_spells.earthquake.description:
As an action, you create a seismic disturbance at a point on the ground that you can see within 500 feet. For a duration of up to 1 minute, an intense tremor rips through the ground in a 100-foot-radius circle centered on that point, shaking creatures and structures in contact with the ground in that area.

When you cast this spell and at the end of each turn you spend concentrating on it, each creature on the ground in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone.

- Fissures: Fissures open throughout the area at the start of your next turn after you cast the spell. A total of **1d6** fissures open in locations chosen by the GM. Each is **1d10** x 10 feet deep, 10 feet wide, and extends from one edge of the area to the opposite side. A creature standing where a fissure opens must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall in. A creature that successfully saves moves with the fissure's edge.
- Structures: A fissure opening beneath a structure causes it to automatically collapse. The tremor deals 50 bludgeoning damage to any structure in contact with the ground in the area when you cast the spell and at the start of each of your turns until the spell ends. If a structure drops to 0 hit points, it collapses. A creature within half the distance of a structure's height must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes **5d6** bludgeoning damage, is knocked prone, and is buried in the rubble, requiring a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check as an action to escape. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and doesn't fall prone or become buried.
2014_spells.earthquake.effectSummary: Trigger a massive seismic disturbance within 500 feet that creates difficult terrain, knocks creatures prone, and destroys structures.
2014_spells.earthquake.fullDescription:
As an action, you create a seismic disturbance at a point on the ground that you can see within 500 feet. For a duration of up to 1 minute, an intense tremor rips through the ground in a 100-foot-radius circle centered on that point, shaking creatures and structures in contact with the ground in that area.

The ground in the area becomes difficult terrain. Each creature on the ground that is concentrating must make a Constitution saving throw; on a failed save, the creature's concentration is broken.

When you cast this spell and at the end of each turn you spend concentrating on it, each creature on the ground in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone.

This spell can have additional effects depending on the terrain, as determined by the GM:
- Fissures: Fissures open throughout the area at the start of your next turn after you cast the spell. A total of **1d6** fissures open in locations chosen by the GM. Each is **1d10** x 10 feet deep, 10 feet wide, and extends from one edge of the area to the opposite side. A creature standing where a fissure opens must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall in. A creature that successfully saves moves with the fissure's edge.
- Structures: A fissure opening beneath a structure causes it to automatically collapse. The tremor deals 50 bludgeoning damage to any structure in contact with the ground in the area when you cast the spell and at the start of each of your turns until the spell ends. If a structure drops to 0 hit points, it collapses. A creature within half the distance of a structure's height must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes **5d6** bludgeoning damage, is knocked prone, and is buried in the rubble, requiring a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check as an action to escape. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and doesn't fall prone or become buried.
2014_spells.feeblemind.description:
As an action, you blast the mind of a creature you can see within 150 feet, attempting to shatter its intellect and personality. The target takes **4d6** psychic damage and must make an Intelligence saving throw.

On a failed save, the creature's Intelligence and Charisma scores become 1. While affected, the creature suffers the following effects:
- It cannot cast spells.
- It cannot activate magic items.
- It cannot understand language or communicate in any intelligible way.
- It can still identify its friends, follow them, and protect them.

At the end of every 30 days, the creature can repeat its saving throw against this spell, ending the effect on a success. The spell can also be ended by greater restoration, heal, or wish.
2014_spells.feeblemind.effectSummary: A powerful psychic assault that targets a creature's intellect, potentially reducing its Intelligence and Charisma scores to 1 and stripping its ability to cast spells.
2014_spells.feeblemind.fullDescription:

- It cannot cast spells.
- It cannot activate magic items.
- It cannot understand language or communicate in any intelligible way.
- It can still identify its friends, follow them, and protect them.

At the end of every 30 days, the creature can repeat its saving throw against this spell, ending the effect on a success. The spell can also be ended by greater restoration, heal, or wish.
2014_spells.glibness.description:
Using an action, you cast this spell on yourself. For the duration of 1 hour, you gain the following benefits:
- When you make a Charisma check, you can replace the number you roll with a 15.
- No matter what you say, magic that would determine if you are telling the truth indicates that you are being truthful.
2014_spells.glibness.effectSummary: A supernatural enhancement of your social capabilities, allowing you to treat Charisma check rolls as 15 and bypass truth-detecting magic.
2014_spells.glibness.fullDescription:
Using an action, you cast this spell on yourself. For the duration of 1 hour, you gain the following benefits:
- When you make a Charisma check, you can replace the number you roll with a 15.
- No matter what you say, magic that would determine if you are telling the truth indicates that you are being truthful.
2014_spells.holy-aura.description:
As an action, divine light washes out from you and coalesces in a soft radiance in a 30-foot radius around you for up to 1 minute. Creatures of your choice in that radius when you cast this spell gain the following benefits:
- They shed dim light in a 5-foot radius.
- They have advantage on all saving throws.
- Other creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against them.

Additionally, when a fiend or an undead hits an affected creature with a melee attack, the aura flashes with brilliant light. The attacker must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the spell ends.
2014_spells.holy-aura.effectSummary: A radiant aura that grants chosen allies advantage on saving throws and imposes disadvantage on enemy attacks, while blinding undead or fiends.
2014_spells.holy-aura.fullDescription:

2014_spells.incendiary-cloud.description:
As an action, you create a swirling cloud of smoke shot through with white-hot embers in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point within 150 feet. The cloud spreads around corners, is heavily obscured, and lasts for up to 1 minute or until a wind of moderate or greater speed (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses it.

When the cloud appears, each creature in it must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes **10d8** fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature must also make this saving throw when it enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there.

At the start of each of your turns, the cloud moves 10 feet directly away from you in a direction that you choose.
2014_spells.incendiary-cloud.effectSumma: Create a 20-foot-radius sphere of heavily obscured smoke and embers that deals massive fire damage to creatures upon appearance and at the end of their turns.
2014_spells.incendiary-cloud.fullDescrip:

At the start of each of your turns, the cloud moves 10 feet directly away from you in a direction that you choose.
2014_spells.maddening-darkness.descripti: Magical darkness spreads from a point you choose within 150 feet to fill a 60-foot-radius sphere until the spell ends, which can last for Concentration, up to 10 minutes. The darkness spreads around corners. Nonmagical light cannot illuminate the area, and creatures fully within the sphere are blinded.
2014_spells.maddening-darkness.effectSum: Fill a massive 60-foot-radius sphere with magical darkness that blinds creatures and cannot be illuminated by nonmagical light sources.
2014_spells.maddening-darkness.fullDescr: Magical darkness spreads from a point you choose within 150 feet to fill a 60-foot-radius sphere until the spell ends, which can last for Concentration, up to 10 minutes. The darkness spreads around corners. Nonmagical light cannot illuminate the area, and creatures fully within the sphere are blinded.
2014_spells.maze.description:
As an action, you banish a creature that you can see within 60 feet into a labyrinthine demiplane. The target remains there for up to 10 minutes or until it escapes the maze.

The target can use its action to attempt to escape by making a DC 20 Intelligence check. If it succeeds, it escapes and the spell ends; however, a minotaur or goristro demon automatically succeeds on this check.

When the spell ends, the target reappears in the space it left or, if that space is occupied, in the nearest unoccupied space.
2014_spells.maze.effectSummary: Banish a visible creature into a labyrinthine demiplane, removing them from combat until they succeed on a high-difficulty Intelligence check to escape.
2014_spells.maze.fullDescription:

When the spell ends, the target reappears in the space it left or, if that space is occupied, in the nearest unoccupied space.
2014_spells.mind-blank.description: As an action, you touch a willing creature to protect its mind for 24 hours. Until the spell ends, the target is immune to psychic damage, any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, divination spells, and the charmed condition. The spell even foils wish spells and spells or effects of similar power used to affect the target's mind or to gain information about the target.
2014_spells.mind-blank.effectSummary: A powerful protective spell that renders a willing touched creature immune to psychic damage, mind-reading, divination, and the charmed condition for a full day.
2014_spells.mind-blank.fullDescription: As an action, you touch a willing creature to protect its mind for 24 hours. The spell even foils wish spells and spells or effects of similar power used to affect the target's mind or to gain information about the target.
2014_spells.power-word-stun.description:
Using an action, you speak a word of power that can overwhelm the mind of one creature you can see within 60 feet, leaving it dumbfounded. If the target has 150 hit points or fewer, it is stunned. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.

The stunned target must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, this stunning effect ends.
2014_spells.power-word-stun.effectSummar: A word of power that instantly stuns a creature within 60 feet, provided the target has 150 hit points or fewer.
2014_spells.power-word-stun.fullDescript:

2014_spells.sunburst.description:
As an action, brilliant sunlight flashes in a 60-foot radius centered on a point you choose within 150 feet. Each creature in that light must make a Constitution saving throw.

- On a failed save, a creature takes **12d6** radiant damage and is blinded for 1 minute.
- On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't blinded by this spell.
- Undead and oozes have disadvantage on this saving throw.

A creature blinded by this spell makes another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, it is no longer blinded.

This spell dispels any darkness in its area that was created by a spell.
2014_spells.sunburst.effectSummary: A massive burst of sunlight that deals heavy radiant damage and blinds creatures in a 60-foot radius, specifically targeting undead and oozes.
2014_spells.sunburst.fullDescription:
As an action, brilliant sunlight flashes in a 60-foot radius centered on a point you choose within 150 feet. Each creature in that light must make a Constitution saving throw.

2014_spells.telepathy.effectSummary: Send a private message to a creature within range
2014_spells.telepathy.fullDescription: Using 1 action, you create a telepathic link between yourself and a specific creature with which you are familiar. The target must be a creature that you have met and that is on the same plane of existence as you; The target understands the meaning of the words you speak and the other sensory messages you send. Until the spell ends, you and the target can instantaneously share words, sounds, and other sensory messages with one another through the link.
2014_spells.tsunami.effectSummary: Deal 6d10 bludgeoning damage to a target within Sight
2014_spells.tsunami.fullDescription: Using 1 minute, a wall of water springs into existence at a point you choose within range. At the end of each of your turns, the wall's height is reduced by 50 feet, and the damage creatures take from the wall on subsequent turns is reduced by 1d10; On a failed save, a creature takes 6d10 bludgeoning damage, and it is knocked prone. The wall lasts for the duration; you must concentrate, and the effect ends if your concentration ends.
2014_spells.astral-projection.descriptio:
Using 1 hour to cast this spell, you and up to eight willing creatures within 10 feet project your astral bodies into the Astral Plane. The spell fails and the casting is wasted if you are already on that plane. The material body you leave behind is unconscious and in a state of suspended animation; it doesn't need food or air and doesn't age.

Your astral body resembles your mortal form in almost every way, replicating your game statistics and possessions. The principal difference is the addition of a silvery cord that extends from between your shoulder blades and trails behind you, fading to invisibility after 1 foot. This cord is your tether to your material body. As long as the tether remains intact, you can find your way home. If the cord is cut—something that can happen only when an effect specifically states that it does—your soul and body are separated, killing you instantly.

Your astral form can freely travel through the Astral Plane and can pass through portals there leading to any other plane. If you enter a new plane or return to the plane you were on when casting this spell, your body and possessions are transported along the silver cord, allowing you to re-enter your body as you enter the new plane. Your astral form is a separate incarnation. Any damage or other effects that apply to it have no effect on your physical body, nor do they persist when you return to it.

The spell ends for you and your companions when you use your action to dismiss it. When the spell ends, the affected creature returns to its physical body, and it awakens.

The spell might also end early for you or one of your companions:
- A successful dispel magic spell used against an astral or physical body ends the spell for that creature.
- If a creature's original body or its astral form drops to 0 hit points, the spell ends for that creature.

If the spell ends and the silver cord is intact, the cord pulls the creature's astral form back to its body, ending its state of suspended animation. If you are returned to your body prematurely, your companions remain in their astral forms and must find their own way back to their bodies, usually by dropping to 0 hit points.

2014_spells.blade-of-disaster.descriptio: You create a blade-shaped planar rift about 3 feet long in a space you can see within 60 feet. The blade lasts for the duration of up to 1 minute (Concentration). When you cast this spell, and as a bonus action on subsequent turns, you can move the blade up to 30 feet to a space you can see and make up to two melee spell attacks with it.
2014_spells.blade-of-disaster.effectSumm: Create a 3-foot planar rift in the shape of a blade that you can move and use to perform melee spell attacks.
2014_spells.blade-of-disaster.fullDescri: You create a blade-shaped planar rift about 3 feet long in a space you can see within 60 feet. 2014_spells.foresight.description:
With a casting time of 1 minute, you touch a willing creature and bestow a limited ability to see into the immediate future. For the duration of 8 hours, the target gains the following benefits:
- The target cannot be surprised.
- The target has advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.
- Other creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against the target.

This spell immediately ends if you cast it again before its duration ends.
2014_spells.foresight.effectSummary: Grant a willing creature the ability to see the immediate future, providing advantage on most rolls and preventing surprise.
2014_spells.foresight.fullDescription:

- Other creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against the target.

This spell immediately ends if you cast it again before its duration ends.
2014_spells.gate.description:
Using 1 action, you conjure a portal linking an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet to a precise location on a different plane of existence. The portal is a circular opening, which you can make 5 to 20 feet in diameter, and lasts for a duration of up to 1 minute. You can orient the portal in any direction you choose.

The portal has a front and a back on each plane where it appears. Travel through the portal is possible only by moving through its front. Anything that does so is instantly transported to the other plane, appearing in the unoccupied space nearest to the portal.

Deities and other planar rulers can prevent portals created by this spell from opening in their presence or anywhere within their domains.

When you cast this spell, you can speak the name of a specific creature (a pseudonym, title, or nickname doesn't work). If that creature is on a plane other than the one you are on, the portal opens in the named creature's immediate vicinity and draws the creature through it to the nearest unoccupied space on your side of the portal. You gain no special power over the creature, and it is free to act as the GM deems appropriate.
2014_spells.gate.effectSummary: Conjure a circular portal linking your current plane to another, allowing for travel or the summoning of a specific creature.

2014_spells.imprisonment.description:
Using a casting time of 1 minute, you create a magical restraint to hold a creature you can see within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be bound by the spell; if it succeeds, it is immune to this spell if you cast it again. While affected, the creature doesn't need to breathe, eat, or drink, and it doesn't age. Divination spells cannot locate or perceive the target.

When you cast the spell, choose one of the following forms of imprisonment:

- Burial: The target is entombed far beneath the earth in a sphere of magical force. Nothing can pass through the sphere, nor can any creature teleport or use planar travel to enter or exit. Requires a small mithral orb.
- Chaining: Heavy chains rooted in the ground hold the target. The target is restrained and cannot move or be moved by any means until the spell ends. Requires a fine chain of precious metal.
- Hedged Prison: The target is transported into a tiny demiplane warded against teleportation and planar travel, such as a labyrinth or tower. Requires a miniature jade representation of the prison.
- Minimus Containment: The target shrinks to 1 inch and is imprisoned inside a gemstone. Light passes through, but nothing else can enter or exit, even via teleportation. The gemstone cannot be broken while the spell is active. Requires a large, transparent gemstone.
- Slumber: The target falls asleep and cannot be awoken. Requires rare soporific herbs.

Ending the Spell: During casting, you can specify a reasonable condition to release the target. A dispel magic spell can end this effect only if cast as a 9th-level spell targeting the prison or the special component. You can use a specific special component for only one prison at a time; using it again frees the previous target.

2014_spells.mass-heal.description: As 1 action, a flood of healing energy flows from you into injured creatures within 60 feet. You restore up to 700 hit points, divided as you choose among any number of creatures you can see within range. Creatures healed by this spell are also cured of all diseases and any effect making them blinded or deafened. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.
2014_spells.mass-heal.effectSummary: Release a massive wave of healing energy to restore hit points and cure diseases or sensory impairments for multiple nearby allies.
2014_spells.mass-heal.fullDescription: As 1 action, a flood of healing energy flows from you into injured creatures within 60 feet. You restore up to 700 hit points, divided as you choose among any number of creatures you can see within range. Creatures healed by this spell are also cured of all diseases and any effect making them blinded or deafened. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.
2014_spells.mass-polymorph.description: You transform up to ten creatures of your choice that you can see within 120 feet. This effect lasts for a duration of Concentration, up to 1 hour. An unwilling target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw to resist the effect. An automaton succeeds automatically.
2014_spells.mass-polymorph.effectSummary: Transform up to ten creatures within range into different forms, requiring a saving throw for those who are unwilling.
2014_spells.mass-polymorph.fullDescripti: You transform up to ten creatures of your choice that you can see within 120 feet. This effect lasts for a duration of Concentration, up to 1 hour. 2014_spells.meteor-swarm.description:

- A creature takes **20d6** fire damage and **20d6** bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
- A creature in the area of more than one fiery burst is affected only once.
- The spell damages objects in the area and ignites flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried.
2014_spells.meteor-swarm.effectSummary: Call down four massive orbs of fire to strike specific points within a mile, dealing massive fire and bludgeoning damage to all creatures in large spherical areas.

2014_spells.power-word-kill.description: Using an action, you utter a word of power that can compel one creature you can see within 60 feet to die instantly. If the creature you choose has 100 hit points or fewer, it dies. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.
2014_spells.power-word-kill.effectSummar: Utter a word of power to instantly kill a creature within 60 feet, provided the target has 100 hit points or fewer.
2014_spells.power-word-kill.fullDescript: Using an action, you utter a word of power that can compel one creature you can see within 60 feet to die instantly. If the creature you choose has 100 hit points or fewer, it dies. Otherwise, the spell has no effect.
2014_spells.prismatic-wall.description:
As an action, you create a shimmering, multicolored plane of light that forms a vertical opaque wall—up to 90 feet long, 30 feet high, and 1 inch thick—centered on a point you can see within 60 feet. Alternatively, you can shape the wall into a sphere up to 30 feet in diameter centered on a point you choose within 60 feet. The wall remains in place for 10 minutes. If you position the wall so that it passes through a space occupied by a creature, the spell fails, and your action and the spell slot are wasted.

The wall sheds bright light out to a range of 100 feet and dim light for an additional 100 feet. You and creatures you designate at the time you cast the spell can pass through and remain near the wall without harm. If another creature that can see the wall moves to within 20 feet of it or starts its turn there, the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become blinded for 1 minute.

The wall consists of seven layers, each with a different color. When a creature attempts to reach into or pass through the wall, it does so one layer at a time. As it passes or reaches through each layer, the creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or be affected by that layer's properties:

2014_spells.shapechange.description:
Using 1 action, you assume the form of a different creature for a duration of up to 1 hour. The new form can be of any creature with a challenge rating equal to your level or lower, provided the creature is not a construct or an undead and you have seen the creature at least once. You transform into an average example of that creature, one without any class levels or the Spellcasting trait.

Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the chosen creature, though you retain your alignment and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus listed in its statistics is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus in place of yours. You cannot use any legendary actions or lair actions of the new form.

You assume the hit points and Hit Dice of the new form. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. If you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious.

You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them, provided that your new form is physically capable of doing so. You cannot use any special senses you have (for example, darkvision) unless your new form also has that sense. You can only speak if the creature can normally speak.

When you transform, you choose whether your equipment falls to the ground, merges into the new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal. The GM determines whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change shape or size to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge into your new form. Equipment that merges has no effect in that state.

During this spell's duration, you can use your action to assume a different form following the same restrictions and rules for the original form, with one exception: if your new form has more hit points than your current one, your hit points remain at their current value.

2014_spells.storm-of-vengeance.descripti:
As an action, you create a churning storm cloud centered on a point you can see within sight, spreading to a radius of 360 feet. Each creature under the cloud (no more than 5,000 feet beneath it) must make a Constitution saving throw when the spell appears. On a failed save, a creature takes **2d6** thunder damage and is deafened for 5 minutes.

While you maintain concentration for a duration of up to 1 minute, the storm produces additional effects on your turn:
- Round 2: Acidic rain falls, and each creature and object under the cloud takes **1d6** acid damage.
- Round 3: You call six bolts of lightning to strike six creatures or objects of your choice beneath the cloud. A struck creature must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking **10d6** lightning damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.
- Round 4: Hailstones rain down, and each creature under the cloud takes **2d6** bludgeoning damage.
- Round 5-10: Gusts and freezing rain make the area difficult terrain and heavily obscured. Each creature there takes **1d6** cold damage. Ranged weapon attacks are impossible, and the weather acts as a severe distraction for concentration. Strong winds (20 to 50 mph) automatically disperse fog, mists, and similar phenomena.

2014_spells.time-stop.description:
Using an action, you briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself. While no time passes for other creatures, you take **1d4 + 1** turns in a row, during which you can move and use actions as normal. This spell is cast with a range of self and has an instantaneous duration.

The spell ends immediately if:
- One of your actions or any effects you create affects a creature other than you, or an object being worn or carried by someone other than you.
- You move to a place more than 1,000 feet from the location where you cast the spell.

2014_spells.true-polymorph.description:
As an action, you choose one creature or nonmagical object you can see within 30 feet and transform it. The transformation lasts for a duration of up to 1 hour, or until the target drops to 0 hit points or dies. If you concentrate for the full duration, the transformation becomes permanent. Shapechangers are unaffected, and an unwilling creature can make a Wisdom saving throw to avoid the effect.

- Creature into Creature: The new form can be any creature with a challenge rating equal to or less than the target's (or its level). The target's game statistics, including mental ability scores, are replaced by the new form, though it retains its alignment and personality. The target assumes the hit points of the new form; if it reverts due to dropping to 0 hit points, excess damage carries over to its normal form. The creature is limited by its new form's capabilities regarding speech, spellcasting, and the use of hands. Gear melds into the new form and cannot be used.
- Object into Creature: You can turn an object into a creature of the same size or smaller with a challenge rating of 9 or lower. The creature is friendly to you and your companions, acting on your turns under your control. If the spell becomes permanent, you no longer control the creature.
- Creature into Object: The creature and everything it is wearing or carrying transform into the object. The creature's statistics become those of the object, and it has no memory of the time spent in this form.

2014_spells.true-resurrection.descriptio:
By spending 1 hour to cast this spell, you touch a creature that has been dead for no longer than 200 years and that died for any reason except old age. If the creature's soul is free and willing, the creature is restored to life with all its hit points.

This spell provides the following benefits:
- Closes all wounds, neutralizes any poison, cures all diseases, and lifts any curses affecting the creature when it died.
- Replaces damaged or missing organs and limbs.

If the original body no longer exists, the spell can provide a new one. In this case, you must speak the creature's name, and the creature appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 10 feet of you. The spell has a range of Touch and a duration of Instantaneous.

2014_spells.wish.description:
By spending 1 action, you can alter the foundations of reality. The basic use of this spell is to duplicate any other spell of 8th level or lower without needing to meet requirements or provide costly components.

Alternatively, you can create one of the following effects:
- Create one non-magic object worth up to 25,000 gp, no more than 300 feet in any dimension, appearing in an unoccupied space you can see on the ground.
- Allow up to twenty creatures you can see to regain all hit points and end all effects described in the greater restoration spell.
- Grant up to ten creatures you can see resistance to a chosen damage type.
- Grant up to ten creatures you can see immunity to a single spell or magical effect for 8 hours.
- Undo a single recent event by forcing a reroll of any roll made within the last round, choosing whether to use the reroll or original roll and applying advantage or disadvantage.

You may also state a custom wish to the GM, though this carries a high risk of failure or unforeseen consequences.

Casting this spell for any effect other than duplicating another spell causes severe stress:
- Until you finish a long rest, you take **1d10** necrotic damage per level of any spell you cast; this damage cannot be reduced or prevented.
- Your Strength drops to 3 (if not already lower) for **2d4** days. Resting with only light activity reduces remaining recovery time by 2 days per day spent.
- There is a 33 percent chance you will be unable to cast wish ever again.

- Be no longer than 6 inches in any dimension

- Resistance to necrotic damage
- Hit point maximum cannot be reduced

2014_spells.elemental-weapon.effectSumma: Imbue a nonmagical weapon with elemental energy to grant it a +1 bonus to attack rolls and additional elemental damage.
2014_spells.elemental-weapon.fullDescrip: As an action, you touch a nonmagical weapon to make it a magic weapon. You choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder. For the duration of the spell, which requires concentration for up to 1 hour, the weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls and deals an extra **1d4** damage of the chosen type.
2014_spells.fast-friends.description: As an action, you call on the magic of the realm to make a creature within 30 feet that can see or hear you more amenable to your presence. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature becomes charmed by you for the duration of the spell, which requires concentration for up to 1 hour.
2014_spells.fast-friends.effectSummary: Target a creature within 30 feet to attempt to charm them, making them more amenable to your presence via a Wisdom saving throw.
2014_spells.fast-friends.fullDescription: As an action, you call on the magic of the realm to make a creature within 30 feet that can see or hear you more amenable to your presence. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature becomes charmed by you for the duration of the spell, which requires concentration for up to 1 hour.
2014_spells.protection-from-energy-2.des: You touch a willing creature, and for the duration, that creature has resistance to one damage type of your choice: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
2014_spells.protection-from-energy-2.eff: Grant a willing creature resistance to a specific elemental damage type, protecting them from acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
2014_spells.protection-from-energy-2.ful: You touch a willing creature, and for the duration, that creature has resistance to one damage type of your choice: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
2014_spells.aura-of-vitality.description: As a bonus action, you cause healing energy to radiate from you in an aura with a radius of 30 feet. Until the spell ends, which requires Concentration for up to 1 minute, the aura moves with you, centered on you. While the spell is active, you can use a bonus action to cause one creature in the aura (including you) to regain **2d6** hit points.
2014_spells.aura-of-vitality.effectSumma: Create a 30-foot radius aura of healing energy that allows you to restore hit points to creatures within the area using a bonus action.
2014_spells.aura-of-vitality.fullDescrip: As a bonus action, you cause healing energy to radiate from you in an aura with a radius of 30 feet. Until the spell ends, which requires Concentration for up to 1 minute, the aura moves with you, centered on you. While the spell is active, you can use a bonus action to cause one creature in the aura (including you) to regain **2d6** hit points.
2014_spells.leomunds-secret-chest.descri: Using 1 action, you touch a chest and a replica that serves as a material component to hide the chest and all its contents on the Ethereal Plane. This effect is instantaneous. The chest can contain up to 12 cubic feet of nonliving material (3 feet by 4 feet by 2 feet).
2014_spells.leomunds-secret-chest.effect: Secure a chest and its contents by hiding them on the Ethereal Plane, provided the chest is within 12 cubic feet.
2014_spells.leomunds-secret-chest.fullDe: Using 1 action, you touch a chest and a replica that serves as a material component to hide the chest and all its contents on the Ethereal Plane. This effect is instantaneous. The chest can contain up to 12 cubic feet of nonliving material (3 feet by 4 feet by 2 feet).
2014_spells.greater-transport-via-plants: As an action, you create a magical link between a Large or larger inanimate plant within 10 feet and another plant, at any distance, on the same plane of existence. To use this spell, you must have seen or touched the destination plant before. The link lasts for 1 round.
Establish a magical link between a Large or larger inanimate plant within 10 feet and another plant on the same plane of existence that you have previously seen or touched.

As an action, you create a magical link between a Large or larger inanimate plant within 10 feet and another plant, at any distance, on the same plane of existence. To use this spell, you must have seen or touched the destination plant before. The link lasts for 1 round.
2014_spells.illusory-dragon.description: By gathering threads of shadow material from the Shadowfell, you use an action to create a Huge shadowy dragon in an unoccupied space that you can see within 120 feet. The illusion lasts for a duration of concentration, up to 1 minute, and occupies its space as if it were a creature.
2014_spells.illusory-dragon.effectSummar: Manifest a Huge shadowy dragon illusion in an unoccupied space within 120 feet by gathering shadow material from the Shadowfell for up to 1 minute.
2014_spells.illusory-dragon.fullDescript: By gathering threads of shadow material from the Shadowfell, you use an action to create a Huge shadowy dragon in an unoccupied space that you can see within 120 feet. The illusion lasts for a duration of concentration, up to 1 minute, and occupies its space as if it were a creature.
2014_spells.polar-ray.description: As an action, a blue-white ray of freezing ice streaks toward a creature within 120 feet. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes **9d8** cold damage, and its speed is halved until the start of your next turn. The effect is instantaneous.
2014_spells.polar-ray.effectSummary: Launch a freezing ray at a creature within 120 feet to deal significant cold damage and reduce the target's movement speed until your next turn.
2014_spells.polar-ray.fullDescription: As an action, a blue-white ray of freezing ice streaks toward a creature within 120 feet. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes **9d8** cold damage, and its speed is halved until the start of your next turn. The effect is instantaneous.
2014_spells.power-heal.description: As an action, you release a wave of healing energy that washes over a creature you can see within 60 feet. The target regains 70 hit points. Additionally, this spell ends any blindness, deafness, and diseases currently affecting the target.
2014_spells.power-heal.effectSummary: A powerful restorative spell that restores a significant amount of health to a single target and cures several debilitating conditions.
2014_spells.power-heal.fullDescription: As an action, you release a wave of healing energy that washes over a creature you can see within 60 feet. The target regains 70 hit points. Additionally, this spell ends any blindness, deafness, and diseases currently affecting the target.
2014_spells.summon-draconic-spirit.descr: Using 1 action and a dragon scale as a material component, you summon a draconic spirit at a range of 60 feet. The summoned spirit remains for a duration of 1 hour.
2014_spells.summon-draconic-spirit.effec: A conjuration spell used to bring forth a draconic spirit to aid the caster for a limited duration.
2014_spells.summon-draconic-spirit.fullD: Using 1 action and a dragon scale as a material component, you summon a draconic spirit at a range of 60 feet. The summoned spirit remains for a duration of 1 hour.
2014_spells.bigbys-hand.description: As an action, you use an eggshell and a piece of parchment to create a Large hand of shimmering force within 120 feet. The hand persists for a duration of 1 minute.
2014_spells.bigbys-hand.effectSummary: A utility spell that manifests a Large hand made of shimmering force to interact with the environment or enemies.
2014_spells.bigbys-hand.fullDescription: As an action, you use an eggshell and a piece of parchment to create a Large hand of shimmering force within 120 feet. The hand persists for a duration of 1 minute.
